review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–229) and looked only at its simp interface. It has one simp attribute: `@[scoped simp] coe_restrictLevel` (`⇑(restrictLevel h f) = ⇑f`). That lemma is proved by `rfl`, its direction is correct, it is guarded by a scoped namespace, and it can't loop. The other lemmas (`rescale_apply`, `qCoeff_rescale`, `qCoeff_sub_smul`, `diagMatInt_map_eq`, `heckeDiagMatrixQ_map`, `exists_cocycle_*`) are used only through explicit `rw`, `have` or `exact`. I found no sign that they need simp attributes. `qCoeff_rescale` has an `ite` right-hand side and `rescale_apply` rewrites to a smul expression, so tagging them simp could cause unwanted expansion. The `simp` calls inside proofs are ordinary and don't expose problems with the interface. A `qCoeff_restrictLevel` simp lemma would be possible, but it is used once, by `rfl` in `main`, so I couldn't justify it under the rubric. I did not run Lean, and I did not check downstream files outside this one for simp uses of these declarations. That leaves some uncertainty.
